messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant that solves tasks step by step.

Task Guide: Task: Simulate uniaxial tensile loading of an Aluminum single crystal using LAMMPS. The crystal should be oriented such that the simulation box axes x, y, and z align with the crystallographic <100> directions of the face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice. Use metal units and define an FCC lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Construct a 10×10×10 unit cell simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. Equilibrate the system at 300 K and zero pressure isotropically using the NPT ensemble with a Nose-Hoover thermostat and barostat. Use a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds and run equilibration for at least 20 picoseconds. Following equilibration, apply uniaxial tensile deformation along the x-axis at a strain rate of 0.01 ps⁻¹ by deforming the simulation box in the x-direction, while maintaining zero pressure in the transverse y and z directions via NPT dynamics. Continue deformation for 20 picoseconds to capture the material’s mechanical response. Record the strain and corresponding stress components in the format `strain, stress_xx, stress_yy, stress_zz` every 100 timesteps, with stresses saved in GPa. As the final result, report the maximum tensile stress (in GPa) along the x-direction achieved prior to the onset of plastic deformation or structural instability, identified as the first significant drop in the stress-strain response. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/claude_35/brief/task_8/task_8_trial_2 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.
